svg.aria-label: What happened: the child's chromosomes as the reads hold them, and where HPRC's assembly put each piece

path.title: M holds one copy's sequence. The two maternal copies are identical outside one stretch and no read spans a copy, so the two were read as one (a collapse); where the other copy is in no piece, its reads pile onto M
M runs from its one copy straight into the right flank: the other copy, and the junction, are not in it
A: the father's sequence, chr2:46,970,725-47,340,307, in his chromosome
B: the mother's sequence - chr2:46,971,835-47,340,686 of her other copy - in the father's chromosome 279 of her own alleles, none of his; base for base M
C: the father's sequence, chr2:47,319,800-47,774,341, in his chromosome
D: the mother's sequence - chr2:47,755,434-48,055,872 of her other copy - in the father's chromosome 3 of her own alleles, none of his; base for base M
E: the father's sequence, chr2:47,756,575-48,057,041, in his chromosome
U holds this part of the other copy, where the two maternal copies differ; it has no place in either chromosome

1 The two maternal copies collapsed into one, M. 2 Pieces of the other copy, B and D, put in the father's chromosome; U left without a place.
3 Joined across 100-N gaps no read crosses. 4 187 kb of the other copy, and the junction, in no piece. 5 The father's pieces overlap.
To scale, the flanks (100 kb) faint. HPRC's paternal chromosome is drawn piece by piece in its own order, a black mark at each gap; colours by each piece's alleles.
